method: First-hand: every licence line below was fetched from this environment (huggingface.co dataset cards / openslr.org pages) with the URL given, on 2026-10-11. Where a card declares no licence, the upstream origin is named and marked 'not declared here'. Nothing in this file is quoted from memory.
noAudioCommitted: No corpus audio is committed to the repo (see .gitignore: real/, data/). The repo carries the fetch script, the source ids and this licence review. Both EVAL corpora below are marked 'eval-only' and are not redistributed.

evalCorpora.note: The two corpora this task actually scored (AC2). They are held-out evaluation sources, not training sources.

entries.usedAs: real Chinese speech — SCRIPTED single-utterance reads (reported separately, never merged)
entries.licenceTextFirstHand: OpenSLR page prints 'License: Apache License v.2.0'.
entries.licenceSpdx: Apache-2.0 (per OpenSLR) — with a noted ambiguity
entries.ambiguity: CSLT's own prose elsewhere describes THCHS-30 as 'totally free to academic users', which is a NARROWER grant than Apache-2.0. The two statements disagree.
entries.verdict: eval-only; audio NOT redistributed. Usable for a local research evaluation either way; redistribution would be unsafe under the narrower reading.
entries.redistribution: not clearly permitted (do not commit audio)

entries.usedAs: real Chinese speech — NATURAL spontaneous dialogue (the AC2 primary; gated to clips carrying >= 200 ms real trailing silence)
entries.origin: HKUST CAiRE — spontaneous Mandarin/English code-switched conversation
entries.caveat: CODE-SWITCHED: rows are labelled zh / en / mixed; this task kept rows labelled zh or mixed, so a fraction of each retained clip is English. That is a property of the audio, not of the label — see CONCLUSION.md.
entries.verdict: eval-only; audio NOT redistributed. Share-alike would attach to any redistributed derived sample.
entries.redistribution: permitted with attribution + share-alike (audio still not committed)

trainingCandidates.note: AC5 — candidate Chinese corpora for a FUTURE fine-tune/LoRA. NONE was downloaded or trained on. Ordered by suitability for endpointing (real conversational speech first).

entries.structure: per-meeting .flac (~286 MB each) + test/TextGrid/*.TextGrid per-speaker IntervalTiers with utterance text/timestamps + *.rttm diarization — real turn boundaries in pure Mandarin
entries.access: non-gated; individual files resolvable via /resolve/main/... ; the viewer rows endpoint is flaky (501)
entries.verdict: BEST overall candidate: pure Mandarin, natural meetings, cleanest licence (redistribution allowed).
entries.caveat: large per-meeting files; overlap-heavy meetings (multi-speaker) complicate a single-speaker EOT label

entries.licenceTextFirstHand: README prints 'license: other' with the line: 'This subset is for research evaluation. The original AliMeeting license still applies.' Upstream AliMeeting (OpenSLR 119) prints 'License: CC BY-SA 4.0'.
entries.structure: 3160 row-accessible utterance clips with session_id / speakers / duration / text / overlap_ratio; audio via repo mix.wav (8 kHz)
entries.access: rows API paginates cleanly; audio via repo resolve
entries.verdict: good row-API candidate; 8 kHz is below the 16 kHz the models expect (upsampling loses nothing the 4 kHz low-pass keeps for turn-1-mini, but it is a caveat for Smart Turn).
SCRIPTED reads — acceptable as an acoustic/robustness source, weak as a turn-taking source (no natural turn structure)

entries.licenceTextFirstHand: card states academic research only, no commercial use.
entries.verdict: usable for internal research but NOT redistributable and not commercially clean — a poor base for a shipped fine-tune
REJECT for endpointing training: the audio is synthesized, so its silences are TTS artifacts, not human turn-taking
gated + distributed as very large tarballs with no row audio — impractical for a bounded study

assetsReusedVerbatim.note: Checkpoints reused from P0.13 at the SAME pinned revisions (AC1). No version re-selected here.
